headline: Approved $200,000 for Dorset Commons improvements and a $35,000 Homeland Security grant; staff will review city power over building energy.
summary: Items 12 through 17 were moved to a future meeting, partly because of tomorrow's election. Housing targets were discussed with the regional planning commission, and a joint housing study was endorsed. Staff plans a November 16 package on East Terrace parking, including higher ticket fines.
decisions: Postponed agenda items 12 through 17 to a future meeting.
Approved consent agenda items 6a, 6c, and 6d, covering financial warrants, plowing agreements, and a Development Review Board appointment.
Approved applying for a $35,000 FY 2026 State Homeland Security Grant to help fund the city's emergency operations plan, with one member voting no.
Approved allocating $200,000 from the Housing Trust Fund to the Champlain Housing Trust Dorset Commons project, unanimously.
Endorsed a joint housing needs assessment and action plan with the Chittenden County Regional Planning Commission, unanimously.
Asked staff to review what authority the city has over energy systems in existing buildings, passed 3 to 2.
discussion: Homeland Security grant: A member warned that federal election-security conditions had been attached to similar grants in other cities. Staff said the grant would fund emergency plan work and that no such conditions were in the application.

Housing targets: Discussion focused on whether the 2050 targets matched population forecasts and whether the high range was realistic. Speakers also questioned whether new homes would reach people who cannot afford them.

East Terrace parking: Residents said cars parked on both sides of the street blocked snow plowing and created safety concerns. Staff said a package on parking fines and rules was planned for November 16.

Building energy authority: Members debated whether the city can regulate heating and energy in existing buildings, and whether added costs would hurt renters. Some argued that the long-run cost of inaction is higher.
